{{Short description|Geometric phenomenon}}
[[File:Hart Circle Picture created with Autocad.png|thumb|The circle H touches the incircles I, <math>I_A</math>,<math>I_B</math>,<math>I_C</math> of a circular triangle ABC and its associated triangles.]]
In geometry, the '''Hart circle''' is derived from three given circles that cross pairwise to form eight [[circular triangle]]s. For any one of these eight triangles, and its three neighboring triangles, there exists a '''Hart circle''', tangent to the [[inscribed circle]]s of these four circular triangles. Thus, the three given circles have eight Hart circles associated with them. The Hart circles are named after their discover, [[Andrew Searle Hart]]. They can be seen as analogous to the [[nine-point circle]] of straight-sided triangles.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Coolidge |first=Julian Lowell |title=A treatise on the circle and sphere |date=1916 |publisher=Clarendon Press |isbn=0-8284-0236-1 |location=Oxford |oclc=1017317}}</ref><ref>{{mathworld|title=Hart Circle|id=HartCircle}}</ref>
